the recovery rates of tacyclines were higher than those of sulfonamides and the recovery rates of both antibiotics were negatively affected by the presence of polyvalent metal ions in soil samples.
the recovery of tetracyclin and sulfonamide from soil samples was affected by the metal content of soil.
the recovery rates of tctracyclines and sulphonamides from soil samples were significantly influenced by the metal content of the samples.

the interaction between antibiotics and soil.
the interaction between the soil matrix and antibiotics.
the development of an antibiotic analysis method that is suitable for soil samples with a wide range of physicochemical properties.

the presence of metal ions in the soil samples is the main factor influencing the recovery of antibiotics from soils.
the soil characteristics and the amount of polyvalent metal ions present in the soils have an important impact on the antibiotic recovery rates.
soil properties such as metal contents and organic carbon content should be considered as critical factors for the reliable analysis of antibiotics.

the recovery rates of tectracyclines were not affected by the physicochemical properties, whereas the recovery rates of sulfonamides from the soil samples were affected by the amount of polyvalent metals.
the recovery rates of sulfonamides and tetracyclins are significantly influenced by the cation exchange capacity, the organic carbon content and the metal content of soil.
the recovery rates of sulfonamide and tetracycline antibiotics from the soil samples were significantly affected by the soil characteristics, especially the metal content.

the metal content and the pH of the soil are the most important factors that influence the recovery rates of tacycline and sulfanamide antibiotics.
